events.title: Antonio Vivaldi is born in Venice
events.description: The future composer and violinist was born in Venice. He became known as "the Red Priest" and wrote more than 500 concertos, including The Four Seasons.
events.significance: Vivaldi helped shape the Baroque concerto and influenced later composers, including Bach.

events.title: U.S. Constitution takes effect
events.description: The new federal government began operating under the U.S. Constitution. The First Congress was scheduled to meet in New York City that day.
events.significance: This marked the start of the constitutional system of government that the United States still uses.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is inaugurated as 16th president
events.description: Lincoln took the oath of office as the 16th president of the United States. He took office with seven Southern states having already declared secession.
events.significance: His presidency guided the Union through the Civil War and led to the end of slavery.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt is inaugurated during the Great Depression
events.description: Roosevelt took office at the depth of the Great Depression. On the same day he appointed Frances Perkins as Secretary of Labor, the first woman to serve in a U.S. cabinet.
events.significance: His New Deal reshaped the role of the federal government in American economic life.

events.title: Gary Gygax dies
events.description: The American game designer died on this date. He co-created Dungeons & Dragons, the pioneering fantasy role-playing game.
events.significance: His work launched the modern tabletop role-playing genre and influenced video games and popular culture.
